title: Global ownerMu TryLock in Store.Acquire drops sampled requests despite free capacity
claim: After winning a permit, Store.Acquire TryLocks the process-global ownerMu (critical section: owner scan + clearing 8 writer records ~13 KiB); any concurrent Acquire makes the request DecisionCapacityDropped with free owners. Measured: 15-41% of permitted requests dropped at default max=2, 39-70% at max=64; silent, no telemetry.

title: Exclusive sourceMu TryLock on the read path makes concurrent same-request visitors see tainted values as clean
claim: copySources (every VisitString/IsTaintedString hit, including sink evidence collection) TryLocks the per-slot plain Mutex; concurrent readers of the same request miss each other (0.07%/4.5%/6.2%/19.8% of visits at 2/4/8/16 goroutines; 91-99% when racing source adds).

title: Owner.Finish holds global overflowMu over the full 512-root loop, serializing finishes and truncating other requests' ranges
claim: Finish takes the blocking global overflowMu while clearing all 512 roots (~160 KiB) regardless of use; it is 95-99% of mutex delay in all profiles, and concurrent allocateOverflow TryLock failures silently truncate >10-range roots to 10 (10-14% of multi-range publishes when DD_IAST_MAX_RANGE_COUNT>10).
repro_command: go test -run TestPCOverflowTruncatedDuringOtherFinish -v ./internal/taint/store && go test -run '^$' -bench PCRequestLifecycleOverflow -cpu=1,4,8,16 -mutexprofile=m.pprof ./internal/taint/store

title: By-design shard/owner TryLock drops are small but invisible (no telemetry)
claim: Measured: 0.9-2.1% of requests lose a source to shard contention, 1-4% of derives dropped in tight loops, 0.08-0.17% of reads miss with concurrent writers; owner Counters() and AcquireDrops() have no production caller.

title: Lookup slow path ~16x MayContain cost due to 1.5 KiB ranges.Set copies
claim: Serial Lookup hit ~1.2-1.5 us vs 91 ns MayContain: snapshot reset and several full ranges.Set temporaries copy ~8-12 KiB per owner hit.
